throughput.note: "delivered" counts every work_item_closed event (341 closes vs 126 recorded metric rides) — this includes administrative and non-feature doc closes, not only full agent rides

speed.note: busy_seconds is summed agent duration (agent busy time), NOT calendar wall-clock

cost.usd_note: no USD figure is derivable — tokens_in/out are null across the ledger and the usage marker is an undecomposed total with no in/out split to price

quality.review_verdict_note: per-review pass/fail lives only in prose run notes and is not mechanically derived; only ride verdict + code_review_completed count are shown

Codex P1 on PR #242 (enforce flip): under usage_capture_gate: enforce there is no per-run CLI correction for a run whose usage marker was omitted — append-run only appends, STATE hand-edits are forbidden, so the supported recovery today is the dial toggle (report-only -> close -> enforce) plus the usage_capture=none sentinel for honest gaps.

Factory-report iteration carry: per-series sparkline scaling (same quantity on independent scales, a misread risk needing a spec change), render runs_marked as n= in the weekly cells and tooltips, strengthen the TEST-027 pins (vacuous n/a grep, doc-wide ref grep), and test-aai-metrics.sh dirtying the real tree

a pre-spec gate that can recommend KILL, not only score readiness

the allocator's completion line hardcodes docs/INDEX.md into the regenerated list, so it names the file even when generate-docs-index.mjs is absent and nothing was rewritten

the universal no-regeneration arm never exercises a --reserve that actually allocates

SUBAGENT_CONTRACT forbids subagent STATE writes while the dispatch block explicitly directs them; two roles hit it independently in one ride
the TDD role declares done after targeted suites only, so defects visible only to the full framework sweep surface two roles later and cost a whole validate-remediate lap each
range mode takes added-line numbers from git diff base...HEAD but reads file content from the worktree, so a dirty tree reports an untouched symbol and misses the changed ones
a validation pass survives a later remediation that rewrites the validated code, and the default routing skips re-validation
a validator probe helper ran git commands against the real repository and created two commits on main

EXTERNAL_BIN_WORDS (the .sh/.ps1 external-tool recognizer in D3) is a closed, hardcoded 10-binary list (git, gh, cargo, rg, wrangler, tsc, wsl, sed, npm, npx). A binary outside this list, e.g. grep --color=auto, yields --color as a live candidate instead of being excluded.

The .mjs external-tool exclusion (D3) misses two call shapes: (a) a subprocess call whose command is an expression rather than a string literal, e.g. execFileSync(ghBinOf(opts), [... '--jq' ...]) in hitl-channel.mjs:233 leaks gh's --jq; (b) an argv array built and returned by a helper function rather than a local const, e.g. buildGhArgs() in aai-issues.mjs:235 leaks gh's --state.

the stale advisory prints from the pre-write snapshot on the re-stamp tick, so every fresh validation round emits one false validation_verdict_stale line
TEST-020's corpus scan is polarity-blind and passes only by accident
writing about a control-character escape reliably inserts the control character itself into the prose

scope_cost rows only exist after metrics-flush and the report only regenerates at close, so the section cannot serve the intake's headline motivation (deciding to stop a ride while it is still running)
validation picks its suites from the declared review scope while CI picks them from select-suites, so a CORE suite can be skipped in validation and fail in CI
after pushing a PR the orchestrator stops instead of watching CI, so a failure sits undetected until the owner asks

generate-factory-report.mjs:616 publishes follow_ups.open_count: 0 for an UNREADABLE ledger (e.g. --decisions a directory), the same 'a bad input reads as good news' shape D2 refuses on the CLI; the file's own oldest_age_days convention two lines down already uses null, never 0, for exactly this degradation

requireReadableLedger (follow-ups.mjs:452) uses !st.isFile(), refusing EVERY non-regular file, not just the directory D2 targets; list --ledger <(cat docs/ai/decisions.jsonl) now exits 2 ledger is not a regular file: /dev/fd/N, where it worked before this change (FIFOs, /dev/stdin, process substitution)
the core-sync idempotence assertion discards both sync logs and prints no diff, so a rare failure costs a full investigation to reproduce
file_content_different in aai-sync.sh treats an unobtainable hash as different, so a transient sha256sum hiccup silently rewrites the target's copilot shim and plants a project-overrides file
No guard stops a NEW test or script from pinning a bare 'main' ref that silently never resolves on a pull_request checkout

No mechanical guard remains that a pre-existing arm or assertion in tests/skills/test-aai-deslop.sh is not removed: TEST-027 (test_027_suite_stays_green_and_additive) was mechanized four times, failed independent validation four times, and was withdrawn 2026-08-18, taking the suite-additivity clause of Spec-AC-06 with it.

The PR ceremony ordering - run close-work-item.mjs BEFORE the push, not after - is currently only a habit; nothing enforces it, so a ride can push first and then spend a round chasing framework reds that the close would have cleared.
TEST-005 (no-write proof) never asserts the engine's exit code, so an engine that dies before doing anything passes it vacuously
